title: Validated original-source interval enclosure at corrected row 7
question: Can the exact finite R-419 oscillator/Hamiltonian source be enclosed, propagated through the Gibbs normalization and corrected emission ordinal 7 row, and separated from the R-422 and R-426 reference values without using the rounded graph snapshot?
method: Hash-pin the R-432 ordinal correction and the R-419/R-430/R-431/R-426 authorities, retaining volume 2, cutoff dimension 16, beta 8, right orientation, emission ordinal 7 and parent coordinate 6.

Assemble the source from rational fixture parameters and real algebraic square roots, split it into exchange/global-parity blocks of dimensions 72, 56, 64 and 64, and compute 50-digit point eigendata.

Use directed source intervals with explicit decimal-radius enclosures, residual and Gram bounds, polar correction, and a shifted Gibbs-kernel norm bound; propagate the enclosure to the normalized parent-6 conditional row and fixed core/tail split.

Project the coordinate momentum in the independently enclosed coordinate basis, build the same two-block residual compression, and certify a lower probe with interval Cholesky and an upper probe with an interval Rayleigh quotient.
Run a non-importing NumPy source control, seven hostile mutation checks, Lean R433 scalar checks and the integrated verifier; preserve all uniform and physical promotion flags as false.
finding: The primary original-source lane passes 40/40. Hamiltonian residual and Gram upper bounds are 5.0830027088533099603e-41 and 5.2743084774109142435e-42; the coordinate bounds are 1.1450394871514047264e-43 and 1.3067789239324602381e-43. The corrected row is positive and normalized, and the residual interval matrix width is 6.985088320724423794e-10 below the preregistered 1e-8 finite conditioning threshold. Interval Cholesky and Rayleigh checks give [5.3631875357869327503, 5.3631875357869329910], with bracket width 3.5786932990972513712e-8. The lower endpoint is above R-422 by 2.532836301e-6 and the upper endpoint is below the R-426 direct reference by 8.1426087700902748626e-7. The independent non-importing NumPy control passes 12/12 with finite gap 5.36318775241371; the hostile lane rejects 7/7 mutations, integrated verification passes 13/13 and Lean R433 compiles.
decision_reason: The original finite source is now enclosed at the corrected row and the two fixed reference separations survive the propagated interval. The result is advanced only as a finite source certificate: the residual-basis dependency is recorded by an explicit 1e-8 conditioning threshold, residual reuse remains open, and no uniform, physical or Yang-Mills promotion is justified.
decision_scope: One finite V=2, cutoff d=16, beta=8, right-orientation emission ordinal 7 (parent coordinate 6), exact R-419 rational source, fixed core/tail 7/9, propagated interval residual compression; no cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion uniformity or physical promotion.
boundary: R-433 certifies one finite original-source interval and fixed-reference separation only. It does not close residual reuse uniformly, establish a common core, identify a physical-empty branch, prove Reading-H stationarity or transverse stability, or imply C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or a mass gap.
next_action: Repeat the original-source enclosure at a larger cutoff and volume with an owner-approved tail modulus; keep the corrected ordinal contract and require the same interval, independent, hostile and Lean gates.

adversarial_review.check: Exact radical source expressions, explicit eigendata decimal radii, residual/Gram bounds and polar correction are checked before Gibbs propagation.
Interval dependency widens the residual compression to 6.985088320724423794e-10; the observed width is below the fixed 1e-8 threshold and both probes retain more than 8e-7 margin.
R-432 fixes emission ordinal 7 to parent 6; primary, independent and hostile lanes exercise the row and both one-sided reference margins.
A separate non-importing NumPy reconstruction agrees at finite control tolerance but is explicitly not an interval certificate.
No common Q3 core, limit order, physical sector, normalized empty branch or Reading-H full tangent is supplied.

no_overclaim: R-433 is a finite original-source interval certificate only. It does not establish a uniform theorem, a physical-empty sign, Reading-H stationarity, transverse stability, Yang-Mills dynamics or a mass gap.
